newsitem.title: UK: RTRS-FOCUS - News Corp to cash in on BSkyB shares.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FOCUS - News Corp to cash in on BSkyB shares.

text.p: Rupert Murdoch's News Corp on Thursday unveiled a plan to mortgage part of its stake in British Sky Broadcasting in a move which would cash in on the UK satellite broadcaster's heady share price.
News Corp plans to sell $1 billion of preferred securities for the purchase of stock in its 40-percent-owned BSkyB.
Under the plan, institutional investors could purchase securities and warrants to buy ordinary shares or American Depositary Shares (ADSs) in the satellite broadcaster.
"It shows that Murdoch obviously thinks the (share) value is quite high at the moment to be doing it at this time," said Jason Crisp, analyst at SocGen.
However, Murdoch was expected to keep his holdings in BSkyB through a provision that would enable News Corp to pay cash in lieu of BSkyB shares at the time of redemption.
"That's why I think the convertible is worked in such a way that it is redeemable in five years," said Nick Ward, an analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing.

"Murdoch hopes to have enough return from the cash to be able to redeem the shares in cash," he added, noting that News Corp was expected to use the funds from the deal to finance its television interests in Asia and elsewhere.
News Corp's plan hit BSkyB's stock, which fell 28.5 pence to 607.5 in heavy morning trade.
The fall extended BSkyB's decline since it hit a record high of 698 pence on Monday.
It also capped a week of setbacks, including a negative regulatory ruling and a giant cable merger involving the British units of NYNEX Corp, Cable and Wireless, and Bell Canada International.
Murdoch's move was expected to put further pressure on BSkyB shares, which have been trading at a price-earnings multiple of roughly twice the market average.
"It's one more bit that's going to affect sympathy," said SocGen's Crisp.
"It is an excellent company and doing quite well. But the rating really hasn't taken into account a number of risk factors which inevitably face the company over the next couple of years," he added.
Such risks included uncertainty about returns from digital satellite TV in Britain, as well as BSkyB's digital pay television alliance with Kirch Group in Germany.
For News Corp, however, the share issue was seen as a smart move that would enable Murdoch to raise financing more cheaply than by borrowing from banks.
"Given the BSkyB share price, it seems an eminently sensible financing move," said Credit Lyonnais Laing's Ward.
